title: Carotid Decision Making
official: Improving Shared Decision Making for Older Patients With Carotid Artery Stenosis
summary:
Carotid artery stenosis is a common cause of ischemic stroke in the U.S. and disproportionately affects older adults. Patients with carotid artery stenosis face a complex set of decisions when choosing a treatment strategy. Patients must choose among surveillance with medical therapy alone, versus medical therapy plus one of three different procedures. Each treatment option has different levels of evidence to support it, some of which are decades old. Each procedural option has different expected periprocedural courses, different recoveries, and different cardiovascular risks. This challenging decision is amplified among older adults, where decisional values are often different from younger patients traditionally studied in randomized or observational studies. A decision aid could assist patients and providers who are navigating this decision, but no decision aid currently exists that includes all the contemporary carotid artery stenosis treatment options. In addition, as of October 2023, participation in a shared decision-making conversation is a Medicare-mandated component of carotid stenosis care, with reimbursement for procedures predicated on the documentation of the conversation with the patient.

The objective of this project is to conduct a single arm open label trial to test the feasibility of using a paper-based decision aid for patients considering carotid revascularization. The investigators will conduct a feasibility trial using the decision aid on older adults who are considering carotid revascularization. The investigators will recruit 50 participants aged 65 or older from the vascular surgery clinic and administer the decision aid. The investigators will purposively sample at least 10 participants that are age 80 or older. Primary outcomes will center on feasibility, and secondary outcomes will center on decisional conflict and regret.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients seen in the outpatient clinic who are considering carotid revascularization versus medical therapy or who were admitted to the hospital and are considering elective carotid revascularization.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who are considering urgent revascularization, those unable to provide informed consent using the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire or those unable to participate in follow-up interview or survey scales due to cognitive reasons.
